title: Shining Soul II
subtitle: Choose a hero and enter the dungeon
summary: Shining Soul II is Grasshopper Manufacture's Game Boy Advance action role-playing game built around exploring dungeons, fighting in real time and developing a chosen character. Eight classes provide different starting abilities and equipment choices, while a link cable allows companions to join the expedition. The Shining setting becomes the home of a compact loot-driven adventure, where another weapon or improved skill can change how the next room is approached. Its appeal develops through repeated expeditions, connecting the immediate rhythm of an attack with the longer process of building a capable individual hero.
body: Shining Soul II is Grasshopper Manufacture's Game Boy Advance action role-playing game built around exploring dungeons, fighting in real time and developing a chosen character. Eight classes provide different starting abilities and equipment choices, while a link cable allows companions to join the expedition. The Shining setting becomes the home of a compact loot-driven adventure, where another weapon or improved skill can change how the next room is approached. Its appeal develops through repeated expeditions, connecting the immediate rhythm of an attack with the longer process of building a capable individual hero.

Classes differ in their use of equipment as well as their available skills. A spear can be used as a thrusting weapon by a Warrior or thrown by an Archer, giving the same general item another practical role in a different character's hands. Skills, spells and attributes offer further ways to develop the chosen class. The player can switch between equipped weapons and useful items while exploring. Preparation therefore involves more than collecting higher numbers, because the class determines how that equipment actually behaves during an encounter with the enemies ahead.

Holding the attack button prepares a stronger action, while ordinary strikes provide a quicker response. A Soul item can also be charged through defeating enemies and released for a special effect. These options give a familiar dungeon routine several decisions about timing and resources. Cooperative play adds the possibility of bringing different classes into the same expedition, allowing their strengths to complement one another. The continuing supply of equipment and experience gives each outing a result beyond reaching its final room, preparing the character for another attempt with a different set of practical options.
